brew.title: Coffee Brewing Guides: Every Method, Step by Step
brew.lede: Exact ratios, water temperatures, grind sizes and timings for pour-over, French press, AeroPress, espresso, cold brew, moka pot, Chemex and Turkish coffee — plus how to fix a bad cup.
brew.description: Step-by-step coffee brewing guides with exact ratios, temperatures, grind sizes and troubleshooting for pour-over, French press, AeroPress, espresso and more.
brew.about_h2: How to use these brewing guides
intro: Every guide on this page follows the same structure so you can compare methods quickly: a key-facts box with the starting ratio, dose, water temperature, grind and total time; a numbered method; a dialing-in section that explains which single variable to change first; and a troubleshooting table that maps what you taste to what you should adjust.

If you are new to brewing, start with the French press or AeroPress — both are forgiving and teach you how grind size and steep time change flavor. When you want more clarity and nuance, move to a pour-over cone or Chemex. Espresso rewards the most practice and the best grinder; read the grinder buying guide before you invest.

Whatever you brew, three habits make the biggest difference: weigh your coffee and water with a scale, grind fresh right before brewing, and use clean, filtered water (see water for coffee). Our brew ratio calculator and brew timer do the math and the counting for you.

recipes.title: Coffee Drink Recipes: Lattes, Iced Coffee & Classics
recipes.lede: Café-quality drinks at home: latte, cappuccino, flat white, cortado, mocha, iced latte, Vietnamese iced coffee, affogato and more — each with a scalable recipe card.
recipes.description: Easy coffee drink recipes with scalable ingredient cards: latte, cappuccino, flat white, cortado, mocha, iced latte, dalgona, affogato and Vietnamese iced coffee.
intro: Most café drinks are built from two components: a concentrated coffee base and milk prepared a specific way. A latte, cappuccino, flat white and cortado can all start from the same double shot — what changes is the volume of milk and how much air you whip into it. Learn the milk once and the whole menu opens up.

No espresso machine? A moka pot or a strong AeroPress concentrate makes a convincing base for most milk drinks, and a French press doubles as a manual milk frother. Every recipe card on this site scales with the + and − buttons, prints cleanly, and lets you tick off ingredients as you go.

For iced drinks, brew stronger than you would for hot coffee or use a cold brew concentrate so melting ice doesn't leave you with a watery cup. The cold brew guide and the cold brew vs iced coffee explainer cover the details.

beans.title: Coffee Beans & Origins: Regions, Roasts & Processing
beans.h1: Beans, origins and the science of flavor
beans.lede: Where coffee grows, how processing and roasting shape the cup, and how to grind, store and brew beans so they taste the way the farmer intended.
beans.description: Explore coffee origins like Ethiopia, Colombia, Kenya and Brazil, plus roast levels, processing methods, grind size charts, bean storage and brewing water.
beans.about_h2: Why origin, process and roast matter
intro: Coffee is the seed of a cherry, and its flavor is decided long before it reaches your grinder. Variety and altitude set the potential; processing — washed, natural, honey or wet-hulled — pushes the cup toward clarity or toward fruit and body; and roasting decides how much of that origin character survives.

Use the origin pages to understand what a label is telling you: typical altitude, harvest season, the varieties you will see, and the flavor tendencies of each country. Then use the roast levels and processing methods guides to predict how a specific bag will taste.
Freshness and preparation finish the job. The grind size chart, storage guide and water guide cover the three things home brewers most often get wrong.

gear.title: Coffee Gear Buying Guides: Grinders, Machines & More
gear.lede: What actually matters when you buy a grinder, espresso machine, kettle or scale — feature by feature, budget tier by budget tier, without the marketing fluff.
gear.description: Independent coffee gear buying guides: how to choose a grinder, espresso machine, pour-over kettle and scale, set up a home coffee bar, and clean and descale.
intro: We don't publish sponsored rankings. These guides explain the engineering and the trade-offs behind each category — burr geometry, boiler types, temperature stability, flow control — so you can judge any product on the market yourself and spend where it changes the cup.

The rule that holds across almost every budget: the grinder matters more than the brewer. A consistent grinder paired with a simple dripper will out-brew an expensive machine fed by a blade grinder. Start with the grinder guide, then build out with the home coffee bar setup plan.
Good gear lasts years when you maintain it. The cleaning and descaling guide covers daily, weekly and monthly routines for every kind of equipment.

journal.title: Coffee Journal: Caffeine, Health, History & Culture
journal.lede: Long reads on caffeine, what research says about coffee and health, decaf, history, latte art, sustainability, world coffee cultures and how to taste like a pro.
journal.description: In-depth coffee articles on caffeine, coffee and health research, decaf, coffee history, latte art, sustainability, world coffee cultures and tasting.
intro: The journal is where we go beyond the recipe: the chemistry of caffeine and decaffeination, the history and culture of the drink, the economics behind a fair price for farmers, and the sensory skills that help you describe what you taste.

Health topics are written conservatively and reflect broad scientific consensus rather than single studies. They are general information, not medical advice — always talk with a qualified clinician about your own situation.
Want a weekly digest of new articles? Join the newsletter at the bottom of any page, or browse the coffee glossary to look up any term you meet along the way.
